title: Two Sum II: Input Array Is Sorted

candidate.statement: Given a 1-indexed array of integers `numbers` that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific `target` number. Return their 1-based indices `[index1, index2]`. You may not use the same element twice. Your solution must use only O(1) additional space.
constraints: numbers is sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: The sum of 2 and 7 is 9. Therefore, index1 = 1, index2 = 2. We return [1, 2].

hints: The array is sorted. If the current sum is smaller than target, which pointer can be moved to increase it?
If numbers[left] + numbers[right] > target, moving right leftward strictly decreases or maintains the sum.
short_diagnostics: What is the monotonic relationship between left index advance and sum in a sorted array?

evaluator.rubric: Learner must articulate why inward pointer movement monotonically approaches the target sum and implement O(1) space loop without nested scans.
known_pitfalls: Using hash map (O(N) space) when O(1) space is explicitly required.
evaluator.oracle_notes: Inward convergence works because every step discards an entire row or column of the Cartesian search space.
